chapters.title: Chapter 2714 Meeting Gaia
paragraphs: After the powerful impact, the world fell silent once more... only to be shaken again a few moments later by an even greater force.
This time, the impact was so immense that everyone on Earth felt as though the entire world had been shoved several meters from its original position.
As this unprecedented phenomenon unfolded, countless people across the world believed the end had finally come, plunging cities into panic and chaos.
Finally, after a few more ripples, the attacks ended, the barrier that protected the world remaining intact.
"G-Gaia's prophecy! Gaia's prophecy is coming true! The otherworldly beings have begun their invasion!" one of Gaia's Sanctum soldiers shouted at the top of her lungs shortly after the attacks ended.
Supreme General Tian and everyone around her frowned, but not because they thought she was going crazy.
Practically everyone from Gaia's Heaven believed in Gaia's prophecies, and their expressions had darkened because they were deeply concerned about what was happening.
"We have to return to our city immediately..." Supreme General Tian muttered.
However, before they could move, the Union's representative appeared before them.
"Please return to the conference room! Due to the unprecedented situation, we're ending the break immediately!"

Although he wanted to return to Gaia's Heaven as soon as possible, Supreme General Tian knew he couldn't leave without speaking with the other cities, as they would need to work together to deal with the looming calamity.
A few minutes later, everyone returned to the chamber after having their break cut short.
"What the hell was that just now?!" Rising Sun's representative was the first to speak, questioning what had just happened.
However, nobody spoke a word, but it wasn't because they didn't know what was happening. They had a good idea of the situation, but they didn't dare to voice it out loud.
"I think we all know what that was..." Supreme General Tian eventually spoke.
"Are you going to say that was the otherworldly beings' attempt to invade our world?!" Ember City's representative exclaimed, slamming his fist on the table. "This isn't the time for jokes!"
In response, Supreme General Tian slammed his fist on the table with even greater force, responding in an even louder voice, "This isn't the time to be stubborn!"
"You saw with your own eyes what happened! Our world was attacked! From beyond our sky! How dare you still try to deny Gaia's prophecies?!"
"That phenomenon could have been anything! Did you actually see any invaders?!"
"Haaaa..." Heavenly Furnace's representative sighed out loud.
"Supreme General Tian is right. We need to stop being in denial."

"I am not in denial! Has anyone here actually seen Gaia?! For all we know, Gaia could be an imaginary figure created by Gaia's Heaven to push a narrative that benefits them! I bet they're using this so-called crisis as an excuse to seize control of the other cities!"
RUMBLE!
The world suddenly started shaking again, repeating several times before it calmed down.

Once the tremors finally subsided, Supreme General Tian looked Ember City's representative directly in the eyes and said, "If you don't want to believe it, then don't. Although it would be best if everyone worked together to deal with the invaders from the very beginning, I already expected there to be a few stubborn fools."

He then swept his gaze across the table at the other representatives and continued, "If you're willing to work with Gaia's Heaven to fight the invaders, say so now. Even if you refuse, you'll have no choice but to face reality once it hits you in the face, and by then, you can only rely on yourself to deal with it."
"Spirit City will work together with Gaia's Heaven," said their representative after a moment of silence.
"Heavenly Furnace will also work together with Gaia's Heaven."
One by one, the representatives of each city agreed to cooperate with Gaia's Heaven, including the Union.
Although the Union had sworn never to take sides, the entire human race was in jeopardy, and they weren't taking one side to fight other humans.
In the end, only one party refused.
Unsurprisingly, it was Ember City.
"I need to return home and speak with Gaia first. Once we have a solid plan, we'll let you know how we intend to proceed," Supreme General Tian said.
"That's fine. We'll need some time to deal with our own cities, as well. I can already imagine how panicked they are about the situation right now," said Rising Sun's representative.
The meeting ended swiftly afterward, and everyone immediately returned to their respective city.
Even on their way home, ripples continued to appear in the sky, causing the entire world to tremble.
Eventually, Yuan and the others returned to Gaia's Heaven. However, the place was dead silent, and not a single individual could be seen in the streets.
"Did they all go underground?" Yuan asked.
"Yes, since this is protocol," said Mei Feng.
She then lifted her head to gaze at the ripples in the sky and sighed, "Even though I knew this would eventually happen one day... I never anticipated it would be when I am still alive."
Yuan looked at the sky with her and said, "Seeing how they're having trouble actually breaking into our world, there's still a chance that might be the case."
"You really think it'd take them that long to invade?" Ironwoman asked. "I wouldn't be surprised if they break through whatever is blocking them within a few days."
Eventually, they returned to the military base, and to no one's surprise, the place was in complete chaos, with soldiers rushing about and shouting as though the end of the world had arrived.
After all, most of the highest-ranking soldiers had left for the assembly.
Supreme General Tian then said, "I am going to speak with Gaia. In the meantime, get these idiots to calm down."
"As for you, Captain Yuan... wait for further instructions. I will let you know when Gaia summons you."
"Alright."
Once Supreme General Tian left, Ironwoman asked him, "You're meeting with Gaia?"
He nodded.
"Looks like you'll finally achieve your goal," Mei Feng remarked.
"Looks like it."
Yuan returned to his living quarters while everyone else went to deal with the situation.
When Yuan finally arrived at his residence, he noticed a group of people standing outside. However, they weren't the same soldiers from before. Instead, they were all people Yuan knew well.
"He's back!" Wu Wang exclaimed when he noticed Yuan.
"What's going on?" Yuan asked with a raised eyebrow. "Why are all of you gathered outside my place?"
"The entire base is in chaos, and none of us knew what to do or where to go. Before we knew it, we'd all gathered here," Sergeant Bing said.
"I guess we all subconsciously gravitated toward the place—or person—we felt safest around," Shi Fa said.
"You were ranked second during the drill, after all," Sergeant Quang added.
"Any idea what's happening?" Mei Xiaoyun asked.

"We know just as little as you. It started in the middle of our assembly, so we had to cut it short. That said, the other cities have decided to cooperate with our city to address the situation—except Ember City. They refuse to believe in Gaia's prophecy."
"So it's true... Gaia's prophecy is becoming a reality..." Wu Wang sighed.
"Speaking of Gaia, do you think they'll make an appearance?"
"I actually have a meeting with Gaia later," Yuan revealed.
"Really?"
He nodded.
"In any case, just wait for the military to address the situation. There's really nothing we can do right now but hope the invasion doesn't happen too soon—"
Yuan paused mid-sentence for a moment before continuing, "Actually, there is one thing we can do."
"What is it?"
"I can prepare you guys for the inevitable. I can train you all."
"Training...? That's only assuming we even have enough time for that..." Shi Fa said.
"Then we better start immediately."
"Are you serious...?" Wu Wang asked him with a dumbfounded expression.

Yuan looked up at the sky and said, "I don't know what's protecting this world, but I can tell it's not something that can be broken through in a short amount of time. Still, we don't have forever. Even if we only have a few months, you need to use that time to grow stronger and increase your chances of surviving."
Li Jieyu then said, "I'll vouch for his training. In just two months, I have managed to defeat a Void Guardian in the Orange Zone all by myself."
"What?!" Shi Fa and the others exclaimed in shock after hearing her words because even they couldn't achieve such a feat, and they had more experience and a higher cultivation than she did.
"Follow me if you want to train."
After saying that, Yuan turned around and left, making his way to the training hall.
In the end, everyone who gathered outside his house followed him.
"There's nobody here... I have never seen this place so empty before." Wu Wang remarked as they approached the deserted training hall.
"Who in their right mind would be training during such a situation..." Sergeant Bing sighed.
"Us?" Shi Fa said.
Once inside, Yuan taught Wu Wang and the others everything he taught the Nine Heavens squad—how, by cultivating manually, they could improve their energy reserve and recovery rate.
Then he shared the first three parts of the Limitless Cultivation Technique with them.
However, instead of letting them learn slowly on their own, Yuan shared his knowledge and experience, speeding up their progress.
A few hours later, Supreme General Tian suddenly appeared in the training hall.
"What the hell are you doing here?" he asked.
"Training them."
Supreme General Tian glanced at the others, who were cultivating in silence, before turning back to Yuan.
"Come with me. Gaia wants to meet you."

chapters.title: Chapter 2715 Gaia's True Identity
paragraphs: "Come with me. Gaia wants to meet you," Supreme General Tian said.
Yuan smiled; he'd been waiting to hear those words for quite some time.
"About time..."
He turned to look at the others and said, "You guys can continue training on your own now. If you have any questions, you know where to find me."
After saying that, he left the training hall with Supreme General Tian.
"Anything I should know before meeting with Gaia?" Yuan asked as they walked.

"Gaia may not be a ruler, but she is the most important person in this entire world, so you will treat her as such. I don't care if you disrespect me, but I will not tolerate any disrespect for her," replied Supreme General Tian.
"So Gaia really is a woman, huh?" Yuan muttered after hearing how Supreme General Tian addressed her.
Although Mei Feng had addressed Gaia as 'her' before, she could've said that to confuse him and keep Gaia's identity a secret.
"Do you have an issue with Gaia being a woman?"
"Of course not."
Eventually, they arrived at Supreme General Tian's office, which occupied an entire building.
"Gaia is here?" Yuan muttered as they approached the entrance.
Supreme General Tian said nothing and simply led him inside.
However, instead of taking Yuan to his actual office, he brought him down to the basement, where a single teleportation platform stood.
"Get on."
Once they were both standing on the platform, Supreme General Tian verified his identity using his fingerprints and a retinal scan.
The teleportation device activated shortly after, teleporting them to an unknown location.

After being teleported, Yuan found himself standing on a floating path that stretched toward a circular island in the distance, all of it surrounded by a vast world of myriad colors and flickering stars.
They were clearly in a dimension of its own, detached from the real world, akin to a cultivator's personal world in the Nine Heavens.
Without a word, Supreme General Tian continued forward, following the floating path toward the island.
Eventually, they reached it, where a lone building stood among several trees beside a large pond.
Standing before the pond with her back facing the path was a slender figure in black robes—a black-haired woman.
Yuan raised an eyebrow upon seeing her, as he didn't even need to see her face to tell her identity.
"Yu Rou?" Yuan called out to her.
Supreme General Tian immediately stopped and turned to Yuan, eyes wide, as if he'd just seen a ghost.
"H-How do you know her name?" he asked.
Yu Rou turned around and said, "We've met before. In the hospital."
"What?! Don't tell me you snuck out here and met him?!" Supreme General Tian exclaimed in disbelief.
Yu Rou shrugged, not bothering to elaborate.
She focused her gaze on Yuan and said, "Although you have yet to defeat the Void Hunter, due to the circumstances, I've decided to let you meet with Gaia."
Yuan looked around and asked, "So, where's Gaia? I don't sense any other presence besides you two in this place."
"...You're already looking at her."
"What?"
Yuan stopped looking around and slowly turned to face Yu Rou with a dumbfounded expression.
"You...? You're Gaia?" he asked for confirmation, sounding a bit dazed.
Yu Rou nodded.
"That's right. You don't believe me?"
"I thought you were the Chief of Operations..."
"I'm not foolish enough to reveal my true identity to someone as suspicious as you," she said, shaking her head.
"Anyway, before we get into why I summoned you, let's hear why you wanted to meet with me in the first place.
Yuan fell silent, a puzzled expression appearing on his face.
"What's wrong?" Yu Rou asked.
"I wanted to meet you because you asked me to find you..." Yuan eventually responded.
"What?" Yu Rou muttered, raising an eyebrow, clearly confused by his words.
"I asked you to find me? When? How? I certainly don't recall doing such a thing."

"You contacted me through the system when I was at Gaia's Sanctum trying to clear the 40th floor of Endless Assault, telling me to find you. Hell, you even specifically granted me permission to use Eternal Essence."
Yu Rou's face only became more puzzled after hearing that.

"If I wanted to speak with you, I wouldn't have waited until now to call for you. In fact, I wasn't even aware of your existence until watching your performance during the drill. Most importantly, I do not have the authority to send direct messages to someone through the system, so you must've been mistaken."
"You can't? Even though you're the creator of Gaia's System?"
"It may be named after me, but I didn't create the system. I merely helped spread it," she said, leaving Yuan speechless.
Yuan rubbed his eyes after finally getting a grasp of the situation.
"In other words, the true creator of the system is the Eternal you've been communicating with—the same one who told you about the invasion that would happen in the future."

"Eternal? I'm not familiar with that term," Yu Rou said. "And you're misunderstanding something. I don't communicate with anyone. I merely receive guidance and prophecies from the universe. It's a one-sided conversation, with me being nothing more than the receiver."

"Well, I'm sorry to burst your bubble, but the universe is not communicating with you, and there is a real person—an entity called Eternal behind those messages, and there is more than one of them out there. As a matter of fact, some of them are likely behind the invasion as well."

paragraphs: After a long moment of silence, Yu Rou finally spoke.
"Let's say, for argument's sake, that I believe you. Are you saying that I'm currently being manipulated by an Eternal? If so, what is their purpose? What do they stand to gain?"
Yuan shook his head. "That, I don't know."
"Then let me tell you what I do know. Our city is what it is today because of this Eternal. It didn't merely warn us about the inevitable invasion—it also prepared us for it."

"It taught us about cultivation and even gave us the system, allowing our civilization to advance at an incredible pace. Before receiving the Eternal's guidance, our world was nowhere near this advanced. Hell, we didn't even know cultivation existed."

Yu Rou released a deep sigh before continuing, "I don't know what you've experienced, nor whether you're even telling the truth, but I believe that whatever is behind me is not taking advantage of us."

A moment of silence later, Yuan asked, "What exactly were you told? And when did it start? I assume you called for me because you want me to help with the invasion. I don't mind doing that, but I need to understand the situation fully, as there are still many things I do not understand about this world and its situation."

"I won't beat around the bush," Yu Rou said. "We need your power, and as you've already guessed, we need it to repel the invaders. If you're willing to lend us your strength, I'll tell you everything."
"G-Gaia... That may be—"

"Supreme General, this is no longer a matter of whether we can trust him or not. I didn't tell you this earlier, but I received another message right before the invasion began. It showed me the future—what kind of power the Celestial Beings are capable of, and quite frankly, we're nowhere near prepared for it."
Supreme General Tian swallowed nervously at such words.

Yu Rou faced Yuan with a solemn expression and said, "I started hearing its voice when I turned sixteen. I've never even seen my parents' faces because I was abandoned at birth, so by then, I had already spent my entire life as an orphan."

"The voice taught me about cultivation, making me the first cultivator in the world. Then, it began showing me glimpses into the future. At first, the visions were random and had nothing to do with the invasion, but everything I saw eventually came true.
"Eventually, it showed me the invasion—otherworldly beings descending upon our world, abducting humans, and taking them beyond the sky."
"Although it never communicated with me directly, I could feel its sincere love for us—that it genuinely wanted to protect us. Soon after, the voice bestowed the system upon me."
"Once again, it never told me what to do, but I had a strong feeling that it wanted me to share the system with others... to use it to protect ourselves."
"I created the military and spread the system, eventually creating the world you're in right now."
"What about the Void Specters? Did they exist in the past as well, or did they suddenly appear out of nowhere?" Yuan asked.

"They existed long before I was even born. However, there were far fewer of them back then. In fact, they were incredibly rare. You might only encounter a handful while traveling from one city to another, and those Void Specters weren't aggressive, much like the ones in the current Green Zones."

"However, as time passed, their numbers began to grow, and they gradually became more aggressive... Because of that, travel between the cities eventually became impossible, and we remained isolated from one another until teleporters were created. And once again, the knowledge required to create them was bestowed upon me by the voice."
Yuan pondered everything Yu Rou had told him for some time before finally speaking.
"So, the voice warned you about the invasion and even gave you the means to prepare for it... Yet despite all that preparation and knowledge, you still ended up in this predicament."
He paused briefly before asking, "That vision you recently saw... was I in it?"
Yu Rou shook her head.
"No."
'No? Then either the Eternal couldn't see the future where I showed up, or...' Yuan considered many possibilities inwardly.
"Can you contact the Eternal?" Yuan then asked. "If you weren't the one who spoke to me through the system, then it must've been its actual creator—the voice."
However, Yu Rou shook her head again.
"No, I have no way of contacting them. Like I told you, the communication only goes one way, and I receive their messages at random."
"There's definitely a way to contact them."
"Well, if you know how, do you mind sharing?"
Yuan shook his head and sighed. "Unfortunately, every Eternal has their own method of communication. That said, the next time it reaches out to you, try speaking back to it."
"You think I haven't tried that before? It never responds."
"It's probably because you haven't said anything worth a response. This time, tell them that you know they're an Eternal and ask for their name."
"...I will try," she said.
A moment later—

"Anyway, let's talk about why I summoned you. Although I've already mentioned it, I want to formally ask for your help with our current predicament. I watched your drill, as well as your last fight with the Void Hunter. That ice power of yours... how long have you had it?"
"I've had it even before I arrived in this world," he responded truthfully.
"W-Wait... Are you saying you've always been that strong? That you've only been pretending to improve this entire time?!" Supreme General Tian couldn't help but exclaim after hearing Yuan's words.

"Of course not. I wasn't faking my strength or pretending to improve—at least, not entirely. The power you witnessed comes from a technique that can only be used with a certain type of energy—the very energy from which Limitless is extracted," Yuan revealed.
"Infinity," Yu Rou suddenly said. "That's what we call it."
"Seriously? Even though what you extract from it is inferior and already called Limitless?" Yuan remarked with raised eyebrows.
"We call it Limitless because of its limitless capabilities. As for Infinity... it sounds stronger than Limitless, so..." Yu Rou explained their naming sense with a nonchalant shrug.

chapters.title: Chapter 2717 Level 6 Treatment
paragraphs: "In any case, putting the name aside, Infinity isn't something we're capable of wielding directly." Yu Rou continued. "Are you saying that you can use such power?"
Yuan nodded.
"Are you willing to share your technique with us? If we could wield it, then we have a much greater chance of defeating the invaders."
"It's not a technique. I acquired the ability to wield it after evolving my physique to a certain level."
"Don't tell me... the Perfected Heavenly Refinement?" Yu Rou muttered with a concerned look on her face.
"No, I was able to use Eternal Essence—or Infinity—long before I achieved my current level. However, I wasn't taught how to use it. I just naturally started using it."
"You're telling me that you just started wielding Infinity one day randomly?"
"Pretty much."

After a moment of silence, Yuan asked, "Are you sure no one has ever been able to wield Infinity? What about Tian Yuchen? Or those who cleared the 40th floor and above in Endless Assault? I was only able to clear those floors because I could wield such power."

Since everyone in this world essentially possessed the same physique as him, Yuan wouldn't have been surprised if Tian Yuchen and everyone else in this world had the capability to wield Eternal Essence as well. Otherwise, it made little sense that they had been able to defeat entities capable of wielding it.
'Unless our physiques are not actually the same...' Yuan thought to himself as he suddenly realized this possibility.
Of course, there was also the possibility that his physique had evolved differently from the others, hence why nobody had ever been able to attain the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique.
"None of them could wield Infinity," Yu Rou said, shaking her head.
"So they managed to clear those floors using Limitless alone...? I can't fathom how that's possible," Yuan muttered, looking genuinely puzzled.

Although Limitless was powerful and derived from Eternal Essence, it couldn't compare to the raw energy in the slightest. Yuan simply couldn't imagine how they had managed to defeat Eternal-level opponents using Limitless alone.

Yu Rou then asked, "What made you think Tian Yuchen or the others could wield Infinity? Just because they cleared the 40th floor and above in Endless Assault? Although the difficulty certainly spikes after the 40th floor, it's nowhere near the level where Infinity would be necessary. Otherwise, those floors would be impossible to clear."
"Huh?" Yuan stared at her, looking dumbfounded.
"Even though the opponents could use Infinity?"
Yu Rou raised her eyebrows in confusion before responding, "What are you talking about? That's impossible, and I would know, as I created the place."

In that moment, Yuan realized the Endless Assault he had experienced was different from everyone else's. Tian Yuchen and the others had faced entirely different opponents, and unlike his, those opponents did not wield Eternal Essence.
"You have got to be shitting me..." he cursed under his breath.
"Can you explain the situation?" Yu Rou suddenly asked.

Yuan nodded and explained that the opponents he encountered in Endless Assault could wield Eternal Essence. He even revealed that the48th floor had pitted him against an entity that closely resembled the Void Hunter.

Yu Rou's mouth dropped slightly upon hearing Yuan's experience, and she said, "I don't want to call you a liar, but that's literally impossible, as it's not even programmed to have such capabilities."
The place fell silent as Yuan and Yu Rou stared at each other, unsure what to say next.
Eventually, Yuan said, "Although I can't teach you how to wield Infinity, I can make everyone stronger than before."
"How?
"By making everyone cultivate manually instead of using the system."
"Cultivating... manually?"
Yuan explained, "The cultivation system is extremely effective at gathering Limitless to increase one's cultivation, but when it comes to replenishing exhausted Limitless, it's terribly inefficient.

"If you compared the cultivation system to a water pipe that split into two paths—one for increasing cultivation and the other for recovery—it would send most of the water toward cultivation, even if the person were completely exhausted and desperately needed that energy for recovery instead."
"Unless you can somehow alter the cultivation system and adjust how efficiently it distributes energy, one must cultivate manually to compensate for this major weakness."
Yu Rou sighed and said, "As I said earlier, I didn't create the system. I merely distributed it."
"In that case, everyone must learn to cultivate manually. I have already taught a few soldiers this method, and they've shown tremendous improvements in a short time."

"That's easier said than done. Cultivating through the system is far more convenient, and most people have never even tried cultivating manually once. That said, we'll make it happen." Yu Rou said, turning to look at Supreme General Tian.
"I will make sure everyone starts cultivating manually by the end of the day," he said.
"Hopefully, it's not already too late..." Supreme General Tian sighed.
"Are you responsible for the barrier?" Yuan asked Yu Rou a moment later.
"The one holding back the invasion? No. I didn't even know it existed until recently."

"Is that so? Then it's either a natural phenomenon or something someone else created—most likely the Eternal who's been helping you. And while I don't know how long it'll last, it should keep the invaders at bay for some time."
Yu Rou then said, "Even if the barrier collapses tomorrow, we must do everything we can with the time we're given to prepare for the invasion."
"What about the other cities?" Supreme General Tian suddenly asked. "Should we share this knowledge with them?"

"We're not in a position to be selfish. Since we'll be working together to face this calamity, it only benefits us if they become stronger as well. Even if that decision comes back to bite us in the future, there won't be a future to worry about if we fail to protect this world from the invaders," said Yu Rou.

She then turned to face Yuan and asked, "What about you? Is there anything I can do for you? Since we'll rely mostly on your power, I'll do everything within my capabilities to support you starting now."
Yuan pondered for a moment before responding, "Well, you can increase my Credential Rank."
Without a word, Yu Rou immediately brought up her system to fulfill Yuan's request.
<You have received Gaia's Endorsement>
<Your Credential Rank has increased several levels>
[Credential Rank: 9]
In the blink of an eye, Yuan's Credential Rank jumped to the peak with Yu Rou's help.
"With this, I'll finally be able to get rid of all the curses afflicting me..." Yuan muttered, his voice trembling with a mixture of excitement and nervousness.

Since he could no longer increase his Eternal Essence without first completing his Eternal Constitution, the only other way Yuan could think of to grow stronger was to remove the unknown curses that had been binding him.
However, considering what had happened during his previous treatment, he couldn't help but fear what might happen once he began removing even stronger curses.

It wasn't the unbearable pain that worried him most, either. What truly concerned him was the possibility of losing consciousness and falling into another coma. If it lasted months again—or even years—he could easily end up sleeping through the entire invasion.
"Anything else?" Yu Rou asked a moment later.
"The only other thing you can really do for me is try to get in contact with the Eternal helping you. Other than that... I'll handle the rest."
"Alright. If you need to speak with me after today, you can come back here as you please."
Yuan and Supreme General Tian left Gaia's world shortly later.
Before leaving the room containing the teleportation device, Supreme General Tian had Yuan register his fingerprints and complete a retinal scan.
"Now you'll be able to visit Gaia by yourself, as I'll be too busy to be your guide."
"Thanks."
"Don't even think of doing anything stupid. Gaia may not look like it, but she's unfathomably strong."
"You still don't trust me?"
"I trust you, but I can still be suspicious or wary of you."
"Good enough for me."
"What are you going to do now?" Supreme General Tian then asked.
"I'm going to remove the curses that are still on me."
Supreme General Tian immediately frowned and said, "You won't go into a coma like last time... will you?"
Yuan shrugged.
"I don't know."
"I swear, if you fall into a coma and the invasion begins, I'll wake you up even if I have to waterboard you."
"That's reassuring to hear. Even if you hadn't said it, I would've asked you to do the same," Yuan remarked with a smile—and he genuinely meant it.

After they went their separate ways, Supreme General Tian went to introduce the new training method to the rest of the military, while Yuan returned to his living quarters to prepare for his level 6 treatment.
"I don't care if it's even more painful than last time... Just don't put me into a coma..." Yuan prayed aloud before he began the treatment.
<Utilizing Level 6 Treatment>
<Warning! Warning! Warning!>
[Warning: Level 6 treatment may cause intense pain for the user due to the nature of the anomaly]
[Warning: Level 6 treatment may affect the user's memories due to the nature of the anomaly]
This time, there were two warnings instead of just one.
"Huh? My memories...?" Yuan muttered in a daze, staring at the second warning with a puzzled expression.
The first warning was completely within his expectations, but the second left him speechless and deeply concerned.

That said, we'll make it happen." Yu Rou said, turning to look at Supreme General Tian.
"I will make sure everyone starts cultivating manually by the end of the day," he said.
"Hopefully, it's not already too late..." Supreme General Tian sighed.
"Are you responsible for the barrier?" Yuan asked Yu Rou a moment later.
"The one holding back the invasion?
No.
I didn't even know it existed until recently."
"Is that so?
Then it's either a natural phenomenon or something someone else created—most likely the Eternal who's been helping you.
And while I don't know how long it'll last, it should keep the invaders at bay for some time."
Yu Rou then said, "Even if the barrier collapses tomorrow, we must do everything we can with the time we're given to prepare for the invasion."
"What about the other cities?" Supreme General Tian suddenly asked.
"Should we share this knowledge with them?"
"We're not in a position to be selfish.
Since we'll be working together to face this calamity, it only benefits us if they become stronger as well.
Even if that decision comes back to bite us in the future, there won't be a future to worry about if we fail to protect this world from the invaders," said Yu Rou.
She then turned to face Yuan and asked, "What about you?
Is there anything I can do for you?
Since we'll rely mostly on your power, I'll do everything within my capabilities to support you starting now."
Yuan pondered for a moment before responding, "Well, you can increase my Credential Rank."
Without a word, Yu Rou immediately brought up her system to fulfill Yuan's request.
<You have received Gaia's Endorsement>
<Your Credential Rank has increased several levels>
[Credential Rank: 9]

"With this, I'll finally be able to get rid of all the curses afflicting me..." Yuan muttered, his voice trembling with a mixture of excitement and nervousness.

If it lasted months again—or even years—he could easily end up sleeping through the entire invasion.
"Anything else?" Yu Rou asked a moment later.
"The only other thing you can really do for me is try to get in contact with the Eternal helping you.
Other than that...
I'll handle the rest."
"Alright.
If you need to speak with me after today, you can come back here as you please."

"Good enough for me."

chapters.title: Chapter 2718 Level 6 Treatment(2)
paragraphs: Yuan stared silently at the warnings before him for a long time, a deeply contemplative expression on his face.
Of course, he wasn't debating whether to undergo the treatment; that had never been a choice. Instead, he pondered the possibilities and how the treatment might affect his memories.
Eventually, he stopped thinking about it so much, since it wasn't something he could control.
"Whatever happens happens... I'll leave it to fate..." Yuan mumbled before approving the treatment.
<Treatment has been approved by the user>
<Utilizing Level 6 Treatment>
Almost immediately after the treatment began, an overwhelming pain far more excruciating than what he had experienced last time assaulted Yuan, plunging him into indescribable agony.

Moments later, Yuan collapsed to the floor from the pain. However, he remained conscious as blurry images began flashing through his mind—memories he couldn't see clearly, yet could somehow feel with startling intensity. And those memories were filled with nothing but sadness and hatred.
But he wasn't just gaining new memories. Some of his original memories were being removed too—mainly his earliest memories as Tian Yang.
However, Yuan was in no state of mind to dwell on it, as the overwhelming pain made it difficult for him to even think clearly.
After an unknown amount of time, Yuan returned to his senses and slowly sat up, looking around him with a puzzled expression.
'How long had I been unconscious?' he wondered inwardly.
That's when he felt the ground shake.
'At least the invasion hasn't happened yet.'
Eventually, he stood up and went to the bathroom to wash up quickly.
While he showered, Yuan pondered the effects of the Level 6 treatment.
'Some of my memories are gone... No, that's not quite right. It would be more accurate to say that they've become unclear...'
Most of his memories remained untouched, and only Tian Yang's seemed affected.
'My time inside Han Zexian's cavern is all blurry now. I can't remember what happened after I deciphered the technique...'

No matter how hard he tried, Yuan couldn't remember what had happened after he deciphered the technique on the wall. In other words, he could no longer recall his conversations with Shura, and the earliest memories he could clearly remember were those from after he had left the chamber.
"Did the treatment corrupt my memories or something?" Yuan wondered aloud, hoping that it wasn't permanent and that he'd regain his memories eventually.
While he was in the bathroom, Yuan also checked his appearance to see if it had changed again.
Fortunately, his appearance didn't change at all.
"My appearance didn't change, and I don't feel any different... Just what the hell are these curses, and how are they affecting me?"

Yuan was beginning to question whether removing the curses was truly necessary. After all, if they weren't affecting him in any noticeable way, continuing the treatments seemed pointless, especially when all they did was subject him to unbearable pain and mess with his memories.
"There's a possibility that I won't see the effects until I remove all of the curses, since I still have at least three more treatments to go..." he sighed.
After some thought, Yuan decided to put the next treatment on hold for now.
He left his house shortly after his shower to figure out how long he'd been unconscious, walking to Mei Xiaoyun's living quarters since she was the closest to him.
"Yuan? Where have you been for the last seven months?" Mei Xiaoyun asked after answering the door and noticing it was him.
"It's been seven months, huh?" he muttered.
"What?
"Nothing. I was training in seclusion," he said. "Anyways, what's the situation so far? More specifically, what's everyone been up to for the last seven months?"
"Well, for starters, the Supreme General suddenly made manual cultivation mandatory for everyone. Were you responsible for that?"
Yuan nodded.
"There's no reason to keep it a secret, and it only benefits us if everyone grows stronger before the invasion."
"It's not just our military, either," Mei Xiaoyun said a moment later. "The other cities have also started cultivating manually after seeing how effective this new training method is."
"Anything else?"
"No, not really. Ever since manual cultivation was introduced, everyone has been spending practically all their time cultivating. Nobody even goes out on missions anymore."
"Not even for clean-ups? What about gathering Unknown Ores?"
"Nope. The city has more than enough emergency reserves to last us a hundred years."
Hearing that, Yuan looked up at the sky and asked, "How often do they attempt to break the barrier these days?"
"Several times a week for the first few months, but nowadays, it rarely happens. Once a week if we're lucky."
"Is that so?"
Yuan fell silent, continuing to stare at the sky.
"What's on your mind?" she asked.
"I'm just wondering how much longer the barrier will last, and if I should enter another seclusion since I'll be unavailable for at least another half a year..."
Mei Xiaoyun raised an eyebrow at his words and asked, "What sort of training are you doing?"
"Quite frankly, it's not really training. I've been using the system to treat my curses."
"Huh? Didn't that put you in a coma for half a year last time? Don't tell me you've been gone for the past seven months because of that."
Yuan silently nodded in acknowledgment.
Mei Xiaoyun stared at him with a baffled expression.
"Don't worry. I received permission to do it."
"That's not what I'm worried about. What if you're still in a coma when the invasion finally begins?"
"Then you'll have to wake me up, even if you have to be a little rough."
"Unbelievable..." she muttered. "Can't you wait until after the invasion? Or are the curses really bothering you that much?"
Yuan shook his head and revealed, "The curses don't affect me at all. To be honest, even after removing several of them, I haven't noticed any changes."
"Then why...?"

Yuan let out a deep sigh before responding, "Because I don't have a choice. At my current level, I likely won't be able to deal with the invasion, but I've already reached a bottleneck and can't grow any stronger."
"You can't get any stronger...?" Mei Xiaoyun muttered in a daze, never expecting to hear such words from a prodigy like Yuan.
"Let's just say that there are limitations to my physique, and right now, my only option is to remove the curses and hope it could help.
"In any case, I think I will remove one more curse and see if anything else changes. If not... I'll have to think of something else."
Mei Xiaoyun then said, "If there's anything I can do to help, just ask."
"Alright."
Thus, Yuan decided to do the level 7 treatment. However, he didn't immediately begin and went to look for Yu Rou first.
Some time later, he used the teleporter to go to her world.
"Any news from the Eternal?" Yuan asked.
Yu Rou quietly shook her head.
"But I still have faith in them."
"You know, if they truly want to help us—to protect us—they could directly intervene. Why bother sending you messages like this and leaving us to defend against the invasion on our own?"
"Maybe they're not in the position to help us directly, or... they're not an Eternal like you claim."
Yuan shrugged and said, "No, they are definitely an Eternal. The invaders, too."
"How can you be so certain?"
After a moment of silence, Yuan said, "I know I said that I came from another world... but what if I said that I also came from the future?"
"What?" Yu Rou frowned at such a ridiculous claim. "The future?"
Yuan nodded.
"I wasn't certain at first, but I'm starting to believe that may really be the case," he said.
"The Eternals aren't invading this world to destroy it or to wipe out humanity. They intend to use the humans here as subjects for their experiments."
"W-Where are you getting this information from?" Yu Rou asked with a wary look on her face. "And why are you just telling me this now?"

Instead of answering her question, Yuan asked one of his own, "You said that the Eternal showed you the future shortly after the invasion began, right? What did you see? Did you see the invaders kidnapping humans?"
"I saw chaos..." she replied in a grim voice.
After a brief pause, she continued, "I also saw the invaders capturing humans and taking them beyond the sky..."
"Then that pretty much confirms my suspicions," Yuan said.
'As I suspected, the humans of this world are the original humans—the ones that Eternals had cloned for their own experiments...'
He recalled what Deemo, the Demon God, had told him.
'However, whether this is truly the past or merely a duplicate world similar to one of the Nine Heavens is still questionable...'
"Don't ignore my question. Where are you getting this information from?" Yu Rou asked again a moment later.
"I already told you. I might have come from the future, because something very similar to what's happening now occurred a very long time ago in the world I came from."

Yuan paused for a second, then corrected himself. "Well, quite frankly, I'm not entirely certain myself since I never heard the full story. All I know is that, in the past, the Eternals cloned humans and used them for their experiments. And when I think about how those humans might have been cloned, this situation starts to make sense."
"What happened to those humans? Do you know?" Yu Rou suddenly asked, her fists clenched tightly.
Yuan stared at her in silence for a moment before answering, "From what I was told... they all died."

chapters.title: Chapter 2719 Entering the Level 4 Black Zone
paragraphs: "They all died...?" Yu Rou muttered with a dazed expression.
"How did they die?" she proceeded to ask.
Yuan shook his head.
"I don't know."
"If you're really from the future, you're essentially telling me that there's no hope—that we'll all die from the invasion," Yu Rou said a moment later.
"Well..." Yuan paused for a moment before responding, "Things will be different this time because I'm here."
Despite his words, Yuan's voice lacked its usual confidence. Even he wasn't certain whether he possessed enough strength to repel the invasion.
'I have ten trillion years' worth of Eternal Essence... I should be able to deal with anything that isn't the Void Hunter or Eternals now...'
As this thought crossed his mind, the world suddenly trembled again—far more violently than ever before.
Yu Rou's expression changed drastically, and she immediately summoned a screen displaying the scene outside.
"T-This is...!" Yu Rou clenched her jaw and fists tightly as she watched cracks spread across the sky like a massive fissure.
The barrier appeared to be reaching its breaking point, as though it could shatter at any moment.
However, just as everyone's stomachs sank in despair, the cracks suddenly began to mend on their own. Within moments, the damage completely vanished, and the barrier returned to normal.
"We're running out of time..." Yu Rou sighed.
She turned to look at Yuan and said, "You need to defeat the Void Hunter before the invasion begins."
Yuan raised an eyebrow. "Huh? Why all of a sudden? Defeating the Void Hunter should be the least of our worries right now."

"Although we can fight from within our own cities, that isn't ideal. We need to coordinate with the other cities, and the only way we can gather safely is if you defeat the Void Hunter first," she explained the reasoning behind her request.
Yuan fell silent, as he currently lacked the capabilities to defeat the Void Hunter.
"What's wrong?" Yu Rou asked, noticing his stiff expression.
Yuan sighed, then admitted, "I can't beat it. Not right now.
"I'm not asking you to defeat it immediately, but it'd be great if you could do it by the end of the year—if the barrier can even last that long."
Yuan shook his head and elaborated, "It's not a matter of time. I just can't defeat it... period."
Yu Rou frowned and said, "You were able to make the Void Hunter retreat during your last encounter with it."
"I don't know why it suddenly left, but it's definitely not because it thinks I could defeat it. It also left during our first encounter, and I couldn't even fight it properly back then."
He looked down at his own hands and continued, "I have reached a bottleneck during my last training session, and unless I evolve my physique, I won't be able to get stronger."
"Evolve your physique? It's already at the peak!" Yu Rou said with a frown.
"The peak?" Yuan chuckled. "In the world of cultivation, there is no such thing as a true peak. You can always climb higher."
He turned around and started walking away.
"Where are you going?"
"To fight the Void Hunter."
"What?" Yu Rou's face immediately looked confused.
"You literally just claimed that you can't defeat it no matter how much time you're given seconds ago!"
"That's right. I can't improve my raw strength any further, but there are other ways to boost one's strength."
"That doesn't explain why you're going to fight the Void Hunter right now."
"How else am I going to train? Although the Endless Assault is a decent place to go, it cannot compare to fighting the real Void Hunter."
"Are you going to bash your head at the Void Hunter until you die or somehow manage to defeat it? That's too reckless! If you die before the invasion even—"

"Don't worry, the Void Hunter won't kill me. If it really wanted to, I wouldn't be here right now. It wants something from me, and I am going to bother it until I figure out what. Of course, I don't expect to defeat it, but who knows? A miracle might happen."
"Oh, I don't need any soldiers to come with me. The Void Hunter will probably appear even if I am alone when I approach the Level 4 Black Zone.
Yu Rou was left speechless, and she silently watched as Yuan left her world.
After leaving, Yuan wasted no time, leaving the city and heading straight to the Level 4 Black Zone.

He'd considered doing the level 7 treatment first, but he didn't have enough time, as that would surely put him in a coma for several months, and there was a good chance it wouldn't benefit him anyways.
However, just to make sure, Yuan initiated the level 7 treatment to see what sort of warnings he'd get.
<Utilizing Level 7 Treatment>
<Warning! Warning! Warning!>
[Warning: Level 7 treatment may cause intense pain for the user due to the nature of the anomaly]
[Warning: Level 7 treatment may affect the user's memories due to the nature of the anomaly]
[Warning: There is a small chance the user may die from the treatment.]
Yuan stopped in his tracks upon seeing the new warning, which directly stated that there was a chance he could die from the treatment.
"I could die? How would that work?" he mumbled with a puzzled face.
After all, he could recover even from a destroyed soul—something that would kill anyone else.
"Forget it... I can worry about it later... when I actually plan on doing it..."
Yuan shook his head and continued toward the Level 4 Black Zone.
Eventually, Yuan arrived at the border of the Level 4 Black Zone.

He waited for several hours, but when the Void Hunter still failed to appear, Yuan finally shouted into the distance, "Come out! I know you can sense me! I don't know what you want from me, nor do I care, but I am going to beat you this time!"
Yet, the Void Hunter still did not appear.
After contemplating for a long moment, Yuan decided to enter the Level 4 Black Zone.

"What?" Yu Rou's face immediately looked confused.
"You literally just claimed that you can't defeat it no matter how much time you're given seconds ago!"
"That's right.
I can't improve my raw strength any further, but there are other ways to boost one's strength."
"That doesn't explain why you're going to fight the Void Hunter right now."
"How else am I going to train?
Although the Endless Assault is a decent place to go, it cannot compare to fighting the real Void Hunter."
"Are you going to bash your head at the Void Hunter until you die or somehow manage to defeat it?
That's too reckless!
If you die before the invasion even—"
"Don't worry, the Void Hunter won't kill me.
If it really wanted to, I wouldn't be here right now.
It wants something from me, and I am going to bother it until I figure out what.
Of course, I don't expect to defeat it, but who knows?
A miracle might happen."
"Oh, I don't need any soldiers to come with me.
The Void Hunter will probably appear even if I am alone when I approach the Level 4 Black Zone.
Yu Rou was left speechless, and she silently watched as Yuan left her world.
After leaving, Yuan wasted no time, leaving the city and heading straight to the Level 4 Black Zone.

He'd considered doing the level 7 treatment first, but he didn't have enough time, as that would surely put him in a coma for several months, and there was a good chance it wouldn't benefit him anyways.
However, just to make sure, Yuan initiated the level 7 treatment to see what sort of warnings he'd get.
<Utilizing Level 7 Treatment>
<Warning!
Warning!
Warning!>
[Warning: Level 7 treatment may cause intense pain for the user due to the nature of the anomaly]
[Warning: Level 7 treatment may affect the user's memories due to the nature of the anomaly]
[Warning: There is a small chance the user may die from the treatment.]
Yuan stopped in his tracks upon seeing the new warning, which directly stated that there was a chance he could die from the treatment.
"I could die?
How would that work?" he mumbled with a puzzled face.
After all, he could recover even from a destroyed soul—something that would kill anyone else.
"Forget it...
I can worry about it later... when I actually plan on doing it..."
Yuan shook his head and continued toward the Level 4 Black Zone.
Eventually, Yuan arrived at the border of the Level 4 Black Zone.
He waited for several hours, but when the Void Hunter still failed to appear, Yuan finally shouted into the distance, "Come out!
I know you can sense me!
I don't know what you want from me, nor do I care, but I am going to beat you this time!"
Yet, the Void Hunter still did not appear.
After contemplating for a long moment, Yuan decided to enter the Level 4 Black Zone.

chapters.title: Chapter 2720 The Beginning of the Invasion
paragraphs: As Yuan entered the Level 4 Black Zone, an immense pressure descended upon him like an invisible mountain.
Every entity he sensed radiated a presence comparable to the boss of the 48th floor, some so powerful that he couldn't even gauge their strength.
The humans of this world refused to explore the Level 4 Black Zone for a reason, and the last person to set foot there was Tian Yuchen, but that was over two thousand years ago.
Yet despite the overwhelming danger his surroundings posed, Yuan felt no dread. If anything, he was unusually calm.
However, Yuan moved carefully and stealthily, using Shadow Veil to completely mask his presence as he moved through the void.
'What exactly am I doing...?' Yuan wondered as he ventured deeper into the Black Zone.
He had assumed the Void Hunter would eventually make an appearance, but several hours had already passed since he entered the Black Zone, and it was still nowhere to be seen.
Luckily, he hadn't encountered any Void Specters so far, since he'd been deliberately avoiding them.

His gaze drifted toward the Grand Tree in the far distance, standing at the edge of the horizon. The longer he stared at it, the stronger his desire to approach grew, as though some instinct deep within him urged him forward.
'Since I'm already here, I might as well investigate it,' Yuan thought as he shifted his attention toward the Grand Tree.
In his mind, only two outcomes were possible: either he would reach the Grand Tree first, or the Void Hunter would appear and stop him before he got there.
However, the closer Yuan got to the Grand Tree, the more he realized reaching it undetected by the Void Specters would be impossible, as their numbers increased drastically the deeper he ventured.
Suddenly, the world trembled, and a crack appeared in the sky, prompting Yuan to look up.
A second later, the crack began to repair itself, and within two more seconds, the sky returned to normal.
'What the hell are they even doing? Why attack only to stop and give the barrier time to recover?' Yuan shook his head at the Eternals' puzzling behavior.
He couldn't understand why their attacks were so infrequent. If they had attacked relentlessly, the barrier would have likely shattered long ago.
'It's almost as if they're not really trying to invade—'
Yuan's thoughts were abruptly interrupted when he sensed a sudden change in the atmosphere.
By the time he lowered his gaze from the sky, a familiar figure was already standing a few hundred meters in front of him.
"I was beginning to worry that you wouldn't show up," Yuan said with a smile.
The Void Hunter remained silent.
Even so, Yuan immediately assumed a fighting stance, clearly preparing for battle.
The Void Hunter suddenly spoke.
"You do not belong here..." the Void Hunter said, making Yuan raise an eyebrow.
"You do not qualify to be here..."
Before Yuan could even respond, the Void Hunter raised an arm and pointed a finger at him.
The next instant, Yuan's entire world turned black, as though the void itself had swallowed him.
The darkness lasted only a brief moment, and when his vision returned, Yuan found himself far from where he had originally been.
Yuan looked around and quickly determined that he had been teleported back to the Level 3 Black Zone.
Of course, the Void Hunter had followed him.
"What do you want from me?" Yuan asked.
"Become worthy," the Void Hunter responded, greatly surprising Yuan.

Not only had it given him a proper response, but its speech also sounded different from before. Compared to their previous encounters, it was like listening to someone who had once barely known how to speak but had since become somewhat proficient.
"To become worthy, do I have to defeat you or something?" Yuan asked.
The Void Hunter quietly nodded.
"Then fight me properly. I know I can't defeat you in my current state, but at the very least, I want to know just how vast the gap between us really is."
The Void Hunter remained silent. Although Yuan couldn't see its expression, he could somehow feel that it was contemplating his request.
Suddenly, an overwhelming surge of energy erupted from the Void Hunter, its unfathomable presence instantly spreading across half the world.
Yuan's eyes widened with shock, and his complexion paled.
The Void Hunter's aura was so immense that he couldn't even tell the difference between them!
'That's got to be on the level of a Prime Eternal!' Yuan cried inwardly.
"How the hell am I supposed to defeat you?! You're asking for the impossible!" Yuan exclaimed a moment later.
"That is for you to figure out..." the Void Hunter responded, then suddenly raised its head toward the sky.
Shortly afterward, the world was struck once again, and another crack appeared across the barrier.
This time, however, the damage was far more severe.
If one looked closely, they could even see a tiny hole pierced through the barrier.
Of course, the damage was quickly repaired—but not before several invaders slipped through.
Yuan watched, frowning deeply, as several black dots descended from the sky.
Four.
Yuan counted four of them, and shortly after entering Earth, they scattered in different directions.
'One of them is heading toward Gaia's Heaven!' Yuan cried inwardly upon realizing this.
Without hesitation, he turned his back on the Void Hunter and chased after the invader.
The Void Hunter made no attempt to pursue him and merely watched in silence.
Once Yuan disappeared from view, it vanished into thin air.
Meanwhile, the people of Gaia's Heaven had also witnessed the invaders breach their world and immediately began preparing to confront them.
Sirens blared throughout the base, and as soon as the soldiers heard them, they dropped whatever they were doing and rushed to the Parade Deck, where Supreme General Tian was already waiting.
"The time has come! Gaia created the military for this exact moment! Although there are only four of them so far, do not underestimate them and do not show any mercy!"
The soldiers erupted into thunderous cheers, their fighting spirit surging through the air, mostly because the invaders' numbers were far lower than any of them had anticipated.

chapters.title: Chapter 2721 Fighting the Invader
paragraphs: A few hours after the invaders slipped through the crack in the barrier, the one heading toward Gaia's Heaven finally reached the city.
However, it did not enter the city and instead hovered just beyond the walls.
The soldiers of Gaia's Heaven had been prepared for its arrival long beforehand, and the moment it appeared, they swiftly surrounded it.

Since the invader wasn't in the city, some soldiers had to surround it from the outside, but they weren't worried their large numbers would attract the Void Hunter, since they were still too close to the city walls.
"T-That's what the invaders look like...?"
The soldiers swallowed nervously when they finally saw the invader's appearance for the first time, clear discomfort written across their faces.
The invader had a human figure—or at least something that vaguely resembled one. However, it possessed six limbs: four arms and two legs.

It had a head, but no facial features whatsoever. Its face was completely smooth, and its scalp was entirely bald. Its skin was a uniform, unnatural white, as if it had been coated in paint, giving the creature an eerie, unsettling appearance.
Although no one had truly expected the invaders to look exactly like the ones they had faced during the drills, none of them could have imagined just how terrifying the real thing would be.
Simply looking at the entity sent chills down their spines, even weakening their will to fight.
Of course, its appearance wasn't the only reason. An unfathomable aura surrounded it, radiating a strange energy none of them had ever encountered.
"What are you? And what is your purpose here?" One of the Midnight Squad soldiers questioned the invader.
Unsurprisingly, the invader remained silent.
The soldiers didn't dare make the first move, either.
After all, they still didn't know the entity's true purpose—or whether it was truly an invader in the first place.
However, that doubt was shattered in an instant when the invader suddenly unleashed its energy, killing more than a hundred soldiers in the blink of an eye.
"A-Attack!" someone shouted.
The soldiers immediately retaliated, bombarding the invader with their Limitless.
Yet, despite the barrage, the invader didn't even flinch.
When the attacks finally subsided a minute later, the invader remained completely unscathed.
"N-No way... How are we supposed to fight a monster like this?!"
"Where is Captain Yuan?!"
"Get back! We'll take it from here!" A woman's voice suddenly resounded across the battlefield.
The moment the soldiers heard her voice, a wave of relief washed over them.
A moment later, Ironwoman stepped forward and confronted the invader. But she wasn't alone, and several Midnight Squad soldiers accompanied her.
Ironwoman's aura erupted as she unleashed her full cultivation and struck at the invader.
This time, however, the invader didn't simply stand there and take the attack. Instead, it moved to evade it.
The second the invader evaded Ironwoman's attack, the Midnight Squad soldiers swiftly followed up, striking it with their weapons.
However, their weapons couldn't even leave a scratch on the invader's leather-like skin, much less injure it.
"What the hell?! How are we supposed to fight a monster like this when even high-grade weapons don't work on it?!"
"It must be that weird energy surrounding it!"
"Keep trying! I refuse to believe it's invincible!"
But no matter how many times they struck it with their weapons, the invader remained completely unfazed.
In fact, it ignored them entirely, acting as if they didn't even exist, its blank face fixed on Ironwoman as though it were contemplating something.
After several minutes of complete stillness, the invader finally moved.
It lunged at Ironwoman with all four arms extended, its hands curled into claw-like shapes as though it intended to capture her.
Ironwoman gritted her teeth and fought back with everything she had, unleashing her full strength without the slightest reservation, as though her life depended on it.
Unfortunately, even with her overwhelming prowess, Ironwoman's attacks proved completely ineffective against the invader.
Just as the invader was about to reach her, another presence suddenly appeared and struck it from behind, sending it crashing into the ground with a heavy thud.
Ironwoman turned to look at this individual and immediately smiled behind her mask.
"General Mei!"
It wasn't just Mei Feng, either. General Gu also appeared a second later.
"Where's Yuan?" Mei Feng asked.
"I don't know."
"Damn it! Not even the Supreme General knows where he went!" Mei Feng gritted her teeth in frustration.
"How could he disappear without a word at such a crucial time?!"
"I bet you he never intended to help us," General Gu remarked with a cold sneer. "Hell, I wouldn't be surprised if he was working with the invaders!"
"Save your nonsense for later, General Gu."
Supreme General Tian arrived at the scene with a deep frown, his gaze locking onto the invader, which had already risen back to its feet without a single scratch on its body.
"This isn't an opponent we can leave to the ordinary soldiers. We'd only be sending them to their deaths."

Although it was far from ideal, Supreme General Tian realized that if they wanted even the slightest chance of defeating the invader, all of their strongest fighters would have to work together from the very beginning.
"I can't believe we're already reaching this stage..." General Gu said, shaking his head.
"And there's only one of them right now..." Mei Feng bit her lip so hard that it began to bleed.
"Get ready!" Supreme General Tian shouted as the invader leaped back into the air, then flew at Ironwoman again.
"It's going for Ironwoman again!"
"Don't look down on me!" Ironwoman roared as her aura suddenly flared, becoming so intense that it was visible to the naked eye, flickering around her body like a veil of flames.
She then activated a martial technique, unleashing a wave of flames that engulfed the invader in a sea of fire.

However, a moment later, Ironwoman's eyes widened in bewilderment as she watched the invader absorb the flames directly through its skin, devouring every last trace until not even the faintest flicker remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 2722 Fighting the Invader(2)
paragraphs: After absorbing her flames, the invader continued rushing toward Ironwoman.
"How dare you ignore us?!" General Gu shouted as he waved his sleeves, striking the invader from the side with a powerful martial technique and knocking it down again.
The invader turned its faceless head toward General Gu, sending chills through his entire being. However, it swiftly lost interest and continued going after Ironwoman.
Seeing this, Supreme General Tian shouted, warning everyone there, "It's trying to capture her! Stop it!"
He immediately activated a martial technique, and thousands of arcs of electricity coiled and snaked around his body.
Then his body flickered and vanished into thin air, replaced by a lightning streak that shot toward the invader and collided with it.
Boom!
A massive sparkling explosion erupted on impact, sending the invader flying once again. This time, however, it couldn't simply shrug off the attack, and its movements were seemingly restricted.
The invader's aura surged the next moment, and a chilling, otherworldly shriek echoed throughout the city.
"Is that sound coming from the monster?! How is it even making that noise without a mouth?!" someone exclaimed.
Once the shriek came to an end, the invader moved again, shooting toward Supreme General Tian at blinding speed.
Supreme General Tian tried to evade, but his reaction was just a fraction too slow, and he failed to avoid the attack completely.
"Fuck!" Supreme General Tian cursed out loud as the attack tore through his left arm, his voice in agony.
"Supreme General!" Mei Feng cried out as she attacked the invader, hoping to draw its attention.
However, her attacks had no effect on the invader, so it completely ignored her and continued targeting Supreme General Tian.
Supreme General Tian struggled to keep up, but alas, the invader's speed and prowess were simply too overwhelming. Before long, he lost his right leg as well.
The other two generals continued attacking the invader relentlessly, but none of their attacks seemed to have any effect.
Seeing this, Ironwoman gritted her teeth and shouted, "You want me, right?! Then you'll have to catch me first!"
The next moment, she turned around and fled, flying away from the city at full speed.
Sensing her presence rapidly moving away, the invader immediately lost interest in Supreme General Tian and chased after her instead.
"Stop it! Don't let it capture her!" Supreme General Tian shouted.
"Even if we go after them, there's literally nothing we can do against that thing!" General Gu shook his head, believing it would be pointless to pursue them.
"We should honor her sacrifice and focus on reorganizing the military."
Mei Feng gritted her teeth and clenched her fists in silence. As much as she hated to admit it, she agreed with General Gu.
It was painfully clear that no one there possessed the strength to stop the invader, and recklessly chasing after it would be no different from throwing their lives away.

"Damn it... Where the hell is that bastard when we need him the most?!" Supreme General Tian growled in a low voice when he realized that they had no choice but to let the invader chase after Ironwoman.
"He went to deal with the Void Hunter," a familiar voice suddenly resounded.
Supreme General Tian turned toward the voice, his eyes widening in disbelief when he saw Yu Rou.
Although a veil concealed her face, he recognized her identity at a glance.
"Y-You! What are you doing out here?! You need to go back! It's too dangerous for you to be outside right now!" he shouted at her.
"Too dangerous?" Yu Rou muttered, then replied calmly, "There is no longer a place in this world that is safe."
"Gaia..." Mei Feng called out to her. "What do you mean Yuan went to deal with the Void Hunter?"

"Exactly what it sounds like. I asked him to eliminate the Void Hunter because we need it gone if we want to cooperate with the other cities. It would be unrealistic to defend against the invaders from within a single city, and fighting outside isn't an option as long as the Void Hunter continues hunting us."
"Wait... that unfathomable aura we felt right before the invaders appeared... don't tell me that was actually the Void Hunter?!" Supreme General Tian exclaimed upon realizing this.
Until now, he had assumed the aura belonged to the invaders.
Yu Rou approached Supreme General Tian and held her palms before him, pouring her energy into his body and rapidly healing his injuries.
A few seconds later, once he was fully healed, Supreme General Tian said to the others, "I'm going after Ironwoman."
"But—!"
General Gu tried to object, but Supreme General Tian quickly shut him down.

"Your attacks may not work, but that invader was vulnerable to mine. I'd rather sacrifice my own life than hers. She's still young, and her talent surpasses even mine. I refuse to let someone with that much potential die today—at least not before me."
Without hesitation, Supreme General Tian left the scene, soaring in the direction Ironwoman and the invader had gone.
"Why didn't you stop him?" General Gu turned to Yu Rou and asked.
"I have no right to dictate how he decides to retire..." she responded.
"That invader seemed obsessed with Ironwoman. Do you know why?" Mei Feng then asked.
"It wants to take her to whatever is beyond our sky... As for the purpose, I don't have the slightest clue," Yu Rou replied with a low sigh.
Meanwhile, the invader had finally caught up to Ironwoman right as they reached the Red Zone.
Realizing the invader had caught up, Ironwoman stopped running and turned to face it.
"I could've never imagined that this would be how I die when I left my family and background behind to go to another city..." Ironwoman sighed as she removed her mask.
"But it's still better than becoming a political tool for my family..."
Without a word, the invader lunged at her. However, instead of trying to kill her, it moved with the clear intention of capturing her.
